newsitem.title: UK: Cargolux, Boeing agree early 747F delivery.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux, Boeing agree early 747F delivery.

text.p: Cargolux Airlines International said it has finalised an agreement with Boeing Co to bring forward the delivery of Cargolux's fourth Boeing 747-400 freighter to August 1997 from September 1998.

Heiner Wilkens, president and chief executive officer of the Luxembourg-based airline said in a statement that the 747-400 is "the most economical freighter for long range markets and it has enabled us to eliminate technical stops on many routes."
The 747-400F can carry up to 124 tons of cargo over more than 4,400 miles with the lowest operating costs per ton-mile, it added.
When the aircraft is delivered, Cargolux will be operating an all-freighter fleet of four 747-400Fs and four 747-200Fs, the statement said.
